**Summary:** I implemented F004 (root help agent entrypoint) by adding a shared `root_help_agent_snippet()` helper to `command_guidance.py` that renders a concise "Start here (for AI agents)" block — it names the generated brief (`dontpanic agent brief`) and the read-only JSON guidance surface (`dontpanic agent commands`), and tells agents to inspect recommended actions (`next` / `what-now`) before mutating state or dispatching paid work. The helper projects its command token from the F002 inventory (`command_guidance_by_command()`), so it derives from shared guidance metadata rather than a hand-maintained command list, and raises if the `agent` surface ever disappears. I wired it into `_print_top_level_help` in `cli.py` so it appears at the top of both `dontpanic --help` and the bare no-args usage, deliberately pointing at the brief instead of restating it. I added `test_f004_root_help_agent_entrypoint.py` (8 tests) covering all five acceptance criteria — section presence/conciseness, naming both entrypoints, the inspect-before-mutation rule, sourcing from the shared helper/inventory, and asserting the help does not duplicate the full brief (no brief section headers or the not-IT-orchestration block leak
